findings.evidence: PwC1ImmersionOn.lean:73 defines IsPwC1ImmersionOn and is public-imported at CrossingFiniteness.lean:8; PR description: 'The one-sided tangent limits are the immersion data every later crossing-analysis step of the HW chain consumes.' The lemmas need only ContDiff.Deriv, not the MeanValue/HahnBanach imports the finiteness proof pulls in.
findings.fix: Move exists_deriv_right_limit/exists_deriv_left_limit and their two private interval helpers to PwC1ImmersionOn.lean next to the predicate (adds only Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Deriv there); keep eventually_ne_nhdsNE and finite_crossings here.
findings.issue: IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_right_limit / exists_deriv_left_limit (and their supporting private helpers exists_Icc_right_avoiding / exists_Icc_left_avoiding) are basic API of the IsPwC1ImmersionOn predicate — non-crossing-specific, broadly useful, depending on no later theory. The PR describes them as immersion data consumed independently by later HW steps (crossing angles, exit times, sector decomposition), yet they live in a file titled CrossingFiniteness, forcing future consumers to import the finiteness development to get tangent data.

summary: Imports are specific and all used. The two public one-sided tangent-limit lemmas are general immersion-predicate API and belong in the earlier PwC1ImmersionOn.lean, not in a crossing-finiteness file.
